lines.text: Thanksgiving dinner rose about 6%. First jump since 2022.
lines.say: Thanksgiving dinner rose about six percent. First jump since twenty twenty-two.

lines.text: The Farm Bureau's yearly survey puts a classic dinner for 10 at $58.63.
lines.say: The Farm Bureau's yearly survey puts a classic dinner for ten at fifty-eight dollars and sixty-three cents.

lines.text: It hit a record $64.05 in 2022, then fell three years in a row before ticking back up.
lines.say: It hit a record sixty-four dollars and five cents in twenty twenty-two, then fell three years in a row before ticking back up.

lines.text: So this year's meal is still $5.42 cheaper than that record.
lines.say: So this year's meal is still five dollars and forty-two cents cheaper than that record.

lines.text: The big driver is the turkey: a 16-pound bird went from $21.50 to $23.68.
lines.say: The big driver is the turkey: a sixteen-pound bird went from twenty-one fifty to twenty-three sixty-eight.

lines.text: The Farm Bureau also blames high diesel prices for moving food to stores.
lines.say: The Farm Bureau also blames high diesel prices for moving food to stores.

lines.text: Good news: about a third of items got cheaper, like veggie trays and pie crusts.
lines.say: Good news: about a third of the items got cheaper, like veggie trays and pie crusts.

lines.text: Where you live matters more: the South pays $54.33, the Northeast $61.57.
lines.say: Where you live matters more: the South pays fifty-four thirty-three, the Northeast sixty-one fifty-seven.

lines.text: Hosting? The extra cost mostly sits in the turkey, not the sides.

post.title: Thanksgiving dinner costs more for the first time since 2022
post.ig:
Thanksgiving dinner costs more for the first time since 2022.
The Farm Bureau's 2026 survey puts a classic dinner for 10 at $58.63, up about 6% from $55.18 in 2025.
A 16-pound turkey averages $23.68, up from $21.50.
It's still $5.42 below the 2022 record of $64.05, and about a third of items got cheaper.
South: $54.33. Northeast: $61.57.
Sources: American Farm Bureau Federation (Nov 18, 2026), AP.
News and education, not financial advice.
